title: Round 10 / ECDLP-32: Lean algebraic SLP lower bound for x-only DL computation
question: Corollary of Theorem C (algebraic SLP barrier, x-only, division-free): Let W be short Weierstrass over a field F with 2 != 0, P of order r, 2N < r. Any straight-line program over F of length L using +, −, × and constants, with the single input u = x(Q), whose output equals k (in F) at u = x(kP) for all 1 <= k <= N, satisfies L >= log2((N − 2)/3). Consequence (cost model): if each field operation costs >= c·log p bit operations, such programs need Omega(n^2) bit operations for N ~ r/2 ~ p/2, so the O(n log n) target is impossible in this restricted algebraic model.
claims: Formal (Lean, axioms propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound only): division-free single-input SLP over a field F of length L computing k at x(kP) for 1<=k<=N, 2N<r, satisfies N <= 3*2^L+2 (MathResearch/ECDLP/SLPBound.lean, length_bound_linear_short_weierstrass); also r <= 6*2^L+5 variants (linear order form and k^2 via Theorem B). Bit-complexity consequence NOT formalized.
